entities.summary:
Architecture is the art and science of designing and constructing built environments — from single buildings to urban complexes and landscapes. One of the oldest and most culturally significant human practices, architecture simultaneously solves practical problems (shelter, function, infrastructure) and expresses cultural values, spiritual aspirations, political power, and aesthetic ideals. Major architectural traditions — Egyptian, Greek, Roman, Islamic, Gothic, Renaissance, Baroque, Modernist — mark distinct civilizational moments and constitute much of humanity's most durable cultural heritage.

Architecture's history is inseparable from the history of materials and structural engineering. The Egyptian mastery of quarried stone (pyramids, c. 2560 BCE); Greek development of the column orders (Doric, Ionic, Corinthian); Roman invention of concrete and the arch (enabling the Pantheon, 125 CE); Gothic development of the flying buttress (enabling the soaring cathedrals of the 12th–14th centuries); the 19th-century steel frame (enabling skyscrapers) — each material revolution enabled new spatial possibilities and new aesthetic languages.

Modern architecture emerged in the late 19th–early 20th centuries with the rejection of historical styles. The Bauhaus (1919–1933), Mies van der Rohe's minimalism, Le Corbusier's machine aesthetic, and Frank Lloyd Wright's organic architecture established modernism. The International Style glass-and-steel tower became the default idiom of the 20th-century city. Postmodern architecture (1970s–1990s) challenged modernism's austerity with historical reference and ornament. Contemporary architecture grapples with sustainability, climate resilience, and the relationship between the digital design process (BIM, parametric design) and construction.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Architecture has shaped the course of human civilization through its development of monumental structures like the Great Pyramid of Giza (c. 2580 BCE), which exemplified ancient Egypt's mastery of engineering and monumental construction, influencing architectural styles for millennia to come.
